book_meta.work: short stories by Guy de Maupassant and Anton Chekhov
book_meta.author: Maupassant (d. 1893) and Chekhov (d. 1904)
book_meta.status: public domain — retold from the plots, not from any translation

sentences.ar: كلب زغير عض إصبع صايغ بالسوق.
sentences.en: A small dog bit a goldsmith’s finger in the market.

sentences.ar: إجا شرطي وسأل: كلب مين هاد؟
sentences.en: A policeman came and asked: whose dog is this?
Someone said: it looks like the general’s dog.

sentences.ar: الشرطي قال على طول: والصايغ أكيد استفزه.
sentences.en: The policeman said at once: and the goldsmith surely provoked it.

sentences.ar: واحد تاني قال: لأ، مش كلبه.
sentences.en: Another said: no, it is not his dog.

sentences.ar: الشرطي قال: يا حرام الصايغ، الكلب سايب ولازم يتقتل.
sentences.en: The policeman said: poor goldsmith, the dog is a stray and must be put down.

sentences.ar: وبعدين مرق طباخ الجنرال وقال: هاد كلب أخو الجنرال.
sentences.en: And then the general’s cook passed and said: this is the general’s brother’s dog.

sentences.ar: الشرطي ضحك وقال: يا حلوه، خدوه بحرص.
sentences.en: The policeman laughed and said: how sweet, take her carefully.

sentences.ar: لف على الصايغ وقال: وإنت، بشوفك بعدين.
sentences.en: He turned to the goldsmith and said: and you, I will see you later.
And he went on his way through the market.
